title: Advanced 3D patient-derived glioblastoma organoid-immune cell co-cultures reveal preserved MHC-I tumor cell surface expression and tumor cell-driven T-cell dysfunction
title_zh: 先进的3D患者来源胶质母细胞瘤类器官-免疫细胞共培养揭示MHC-I肿瘤细胞表面表达保持及肿瘤细胞驱动的T细胞功能障碍
abstract: Abstract Introduction Glioblastoma represents an aggressive, immunologically cold primary brain tumor largely unresponsive to conventional immunotherapies. Dissecting patient-specific immunosuppressive cues is limited by current preclinical models. Understanding the functional cross-talk between tumor and immune cells across distinct microenvironmental niches is crucial for advancing personalized immunotherapy. Methods We assessed the immunogenic features of glioblastoma cells and cross-talk with T-cells using bulk and single-cell RNA-seq, multicolor flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry, and functional assays in patient tumors, patient-derived organoids (PDOs), orthotopic xenografts and cell cultures. We developed an advanced 3D co-culture system combining PDOs with human peripheral blood T-cells isolated from glioblastoma patients or healthy donor blood to functionally investigate T-cell behavior in a patient-specific context. T-cell subsets integrated and non-integrated into the PDOs were examined for T-cell activation, exhaustion, and T regulatory cell development in response to tumor-derived signals and hypoxia. Results Single-cell RNA-seq-based crosstalk predicted direct ligand-receptor and soluble axes between glioblastoma and T-cells. Glioblastoma cells in patient tumors and diverse patient-derived models showed cell surface MHC class I expression across diverse genetic backgrounds and microenvironmental niches, modulable by interferon gamma. Subsets of CD4 + and CD8 + T-cells integrated into 3D PDOs deprived of myeloid component. PDO-integrated T-cells were enriched for T regulatory cells (Treg), and exhibited a heterogeneous spectrum of activation and dysfunction states, with differential expression of PD-1, LAG-3, TIM-3, CD45RO, Granzyme B, TCF1, and TOX. T-cells subjected to soluble factors were largely unaffected and retained capacity to reintegrate PDOs at sequential co-cultures. Hypoxia influenced T-cell phenotype, but did not prevent activation or infiltration within the early stages of co-culture. Conclusion Our work provides insights into tumor-intrinsic cues of immune evasion in glioblastoma and introduces a scalable patient-relevant ex vivo platform for functional studies. Surface MHC-I was detectable in all assessed glioblastoma models; and was retained in contact with T-cells, indicating that MHC-I loss is not their predominant immune-escape mechanism. Immunosuppression occurred in direct contact with glioblastoma cells, involving both TOX-dependent exhaustion and TOX-independent dysfunction. Advanced co-cultures of glioblastoma PDOs may serve as a powerful tool for functional studies ex vivo, predicting clinically-relevant responses to immunotherapeutic treatments in the future.
abstract_zh: 摘要 介绍 胶质母细胞瘤是一种侵袭性强、免疫冷却的原发脑肿瘤，对传统免疫治疗反应不佳。由于现有的临床前模型有限，难以解析患者特异性的免疫抑制信号。了解肿瘤与免疫细胞在不同微环境区室中的功能性互作，对推进个性化免疫治疗至关重要。方法 我们利用批量和单细胞RNA测序、多色流式细胞术、免疫组织化学和功能实验，评估胶质母细胞瘤细胞的免疫原性及其与T细胞的互作，实验对象包括患者肿瘤、患者来源类器官（PDOs）、原位异种移植和细胞培养。我们开发了一种先进的3D共培养系统，将患者来源的PDOs与从胶质母细胞瘤患者或健康供体外周血中分离的T细胞结合，以功能性研究患者特异性T细胞行为。我们检测了整合与非整合进入PDOs的T细胞亚群在肿瘤衍生信号和缺氧条件下的激活、耗竭和调节性T细胞（Treg）发育。结果 单细胞RNA测序的互作预测显示胶质母细胞瘤与T细胞之间存在直接配体-受体及可溶性轴。患者肿瘤及多样化患者来源模型中的胶质母细胞瘤细胞在不同遗传背景和微环境区室中均表达细胞表面MHC-I，可被干扰素γ调节。部分CD4+和CD8+ T细胞整合进缺乏髓系成分的3D PDOs。PDO整合的T细胞富集Treg，并表现出激活与功能障碍的异质谱，PD-1、LAG-3、TIM-3、CD45RO、Granzyme B、TCF1和TOX的表达差异明显。受可溶性因子影响的T细胞基本不受影响，且保留在后续共培养中重新整合PDOs的能力。缺氧影响T细胞表型，但未阻止其在共培养早期的激活或浸润。结论 我们的工作揭示了胶质母细胞瘤肿瘤内在的免疫逃逸线索，并提出了一种可扩展的、与患者相关的 ex vivo 平台，用于功能研究。所有评估的胶质母细胞瘤模型均检测到表面MHC-I，并在与T细胞接触时保持表达，表明MHC-I缺失并非其主要免疫逃逸机制。免疫抑制发生在与胶质母细胞瘤细胞的直接接触中，涉及TOX依赖的耗竭和TOX非依赖的功能障碍。胶质母细胞瘤PDO的先进共培养可作为强大的 ex vivo 功能研究工具，未来有望预测临床相关的免疫治疗反应。
